body.statement:
Uniformly over every compact subset of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\),
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
No assertion is made at a genuine tie or for \(|h|>\overline h\).
body.justification: This theorem is the explicit local ATT-absorption phase law on the bounded stochastic experiment.
body.gap: Cardoso, Ferman, and Fernandes (2026) give a strong-signal endpoint; the stable-singleton bounded local transition map is absent.
body.consumer: The law is the primary sensitivity result: whole-sample profiling can absorb bounded local low-rank heterogeneity in a confounding-free oracle class.
body.proof_tex:
The exact finite-array identity is
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
=\widehat x_F-h\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}.                             \tag{20}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}profile}\), the first term on the right is at vanishing distance from \(\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\).  The functions \(\Phi_{NT,h}\) converge uniformly on compact scalar sets to \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), because \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), the singular-value map is Lipschitz, and \(\psi_c\) is jointly continuous, including at \(s=c^{1/4}\).  The tail separation (12)--(15) localizes both deterministic argmin sets.  On a compact subset of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\), uniqueness and the defining separation of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\) then imply
\[
\sup \operatorname{dist}\{\mathcal S_{NT}(h),x_\star(\eta,h)\}\longrightarrow0.  \tag{21}
\]
This is the same elementary separated-argmin contradiction used at the end of the preceding proof.  Finally, the moment assumptions give
\(\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}\to\mu_a\mu_b\).  Substitution of (21) into (20) proves the displayed absorption law uniformly on each such compact set.

The deleted existential clause cannot be deduced from the frozen assumptions.  Indeed, the admissible constants may satisfy
\[
\overline h^{,2}\max\{\overline c,1\}(1-\underline\pi)^2
\bigl(2\overline\mu^{,2}\overline v+\overline v^{,2}\bigr)
<\sqrt{\underline c}.                                         \tag{22}
\]
Condition (22) is compatible with every frozen assumption by choosing the otherwise unrestricted positive constant \(K\) sufficiently small.  It implies the strict subcritical inequality (16) for every \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\).  The proved subcritical theorem then gives \(x_\star=h\mu_a\mu_b\) everywhere in \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\), so no nonempty absorbed subset can exist.  This is a generic admissible-class certificate, not merely a single numerical counterexample.
